one_liner: Research BoringSSL fork that swaps Montgomery multiplication for AVX-512 IFMA residue-number-system arithmetic to speed up RSA modexp.
what_it_does: VROOM is a modular multiplication algorithm that represents operands in a residue number system (RNS) so one large modular multiply is spread across the lanes of AVX-512 vectors. This repository is the CPU artifact for the USENIX Security 2026 paper: a fork of BoringSSL (commit 3fb010b) whose BN Montgomery and RSA code can route multiplication through VROOM, switched on per context with BN_MONT_CTX_set_use_rns or process-wide with RSA_set_use_rns. Callers keep the BoringSSL BN/RSA API; the RNS code itself is C++ templates (Ring<modulus_bits>) under rns/, plus a Google Benchmark binary (bssl_bench) that compares VROOM, BoringSSL and FLINT.
how_it_is_fast: Operands are held in two RNS bases of 52-bit residues and multiplied lane-wise with the AVX-512 IFMA instructions vpmadd52lo/hi (_mm512_madd52lo/hi_epu64), so the per-residue products are independent and fill 8-lane vectors. Modular reduction is an RNS Montgomery reduction: a per-residue Montgomery step followed by two base-extension ('CRNS') matrix products that move the value between the bases, described in rns/vector/batching_vs_no_batching_call_graph.md. Modulus size is a compile-time template parameter, so loops over limbs are fully unrolled, and exponentiation uses fixed-window tables with constant-time selection.
when_to_use: Measuring or prototyping faster RSA verification and modular exponentiation latency on a single core of a CPU with AVX-512 IFMA (tested on Xeon Platinum 8488C, Sapphire Rapids, AWS c7i).
Moduli of exactly 1024, 1536, 2048, 3072 or 4096 bits (the sizes instantiated in BN_MONT_CTX_set_use_rns), for example RSA-4096 verify or RSA-CRT with 2048-bit primes.
Single-operation latency where you cannot batch independent multiplications: VROOM vectorizes inside one modular multiply rather than across eight.
Reproducing the paper's Sections 6.1-6.3 tables with ./reproduce.sh against BoringSSL, FLINT 3.2.1 and the separate OpenSSL and Arkworks harnesses.
when_not_to_use: Production or any security-sensitive use: the README says it is not production-ready, was tested only on random inputs to select functions, and may contain memory errors and security bugs; commit 616817a (2026-05-22) fixed buffer over-reads in rns/vector/changebase.hpp and conversion.hpp.
CPUs without AVX-512 IFMA: the Release build adds -mavx512f -mavx512ifma to all C and C++ flags, so treat the whole libcrypto build as AVX-512-only.
Other modulus sizes: BN_MONT_CTX_set_use_rns prints a warning and leaves the ordinary Montgomery path in place for any bit length other than the five instantiated sizes.
General big-integer arithmetic (arbitrary-size add, multiply, division, string conversion): it is a modular-multiplication backend for crypto, not a GMP replacement.

Builds that cannot pull in GMP and FLINT: CMakeLists.txt stops with FATAL_ERROR without FLINT and includes GMP/FLINT headers into bcm.cc ('TODO: REMOVE GMP DEPENDENCY'), and install_deps.sh says 'The RNS code links GMP for radix<->RNS helpers', although the README says the VROOM code calls only BoringSSL BN_* routines.

integration.form: static lib (BoringSSL fork; RNS core is header-only C++ templates under rns/)
integration.dependencies: BoringSSL build tooling (CMake, Ninja); GMP and FLINT 3.x found at configure time; Google Benchmark for bssl_bench and the OpenSSL harness; Rust 1.86 only for the Arkworks baseline
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 and C11 per CMakeLists.txt; tested only with Clang 21.1.8 (official LLVM prebuilt)
integration.platforms: x86-64 with AVX-512F and AVX-512 IFMA; tested on Linux (Amazon Linux 2023) on Xeon Platinum 8488C, README says c7i-flex.large also reproduces relative speedups
integration.thread_safety: not documented for the RNS code; RSA_set_use_rns(int) takes no RSA argument and acts as a process-wide switch, and the BigInt wrapper keeps a thread_local BN_CTX
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same BoringSSL BN/RSA API with RNS enabled per BN_MONT_CTX or globally for RSA, but only for 1024/1536/2048/3072/4096-bit moduli and only inside this fork; not a drop-in for OpenSSL, GMP or FLINT

gotchas: The BigInt wrapper used to build RNS contexts (rns/precompute/gmp_wrapper.hpp) includes the plain ossl_wrapper.hpp; the constant-time ossl_wrapper_consttime.hpp include is commented out, so precomputation on secret moduli (the p and q contexts in RSA-CRT) may not be constant-time. Not checked further this session.
Ring<modulus_bits> fixes the size at compile time; a modulus longer than the template size makes the constructor print to stderr and abort().
AVXVector::load reads whole 8-lane vectors, which caused the out-of-bounds reads fixed in 616817a by copying into padded buffers; other call sites that load unpadded data could have the same problem.
CMakeLists.txt carries a TODO about large stack frames in the RNS Montgomery code and has the -Wframe-larger-than check commented out.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick VROOM over the truncated batch AVX-512 Montgomery code (lea-gl) when you need one RSA-size modexp faster rather than eight independent ones at once, and over FLINT or GMP-based code when the modulus is one of the five RSA sizes and the CPU has AVX-512 IFMA; for BLS12-381 or non-RSA moduli the authors' separate standalone repository (SimonLangowski/VROOM, MIT) is the better starting point, and CGBN only wins if a GPU is available.
verified_claims_summary: The repository prints no figures; it says the relative speedup over each baseline is the paper's claim and provides ./reproduce.sh, which runs bssl_bench pinned with taskset to core 0 (Clang 21.1.8, CMake Release -O3 plus -mavx512f -mavx512ifma, Xeon Platinum 8488C) for VROOM, BoringSSL BN_mod_mul_montgomery and FLINT 3.2.1, with OpenSSL and Arkworks in separate harnesses. Search summaries of the paper abstract (eprint 2026/393, not opened because the host is blocked) report 4.0x faster RSA-4096 verification over OpenSSL and, from the verifier's earlier search, 1.3x faster signing; two summaries disagree on the BLS figure (3.43x versus 4.05x), and BLS is not in this repository.
status_note: Active research artifact (last commit 2026-06-18, 11 commits, 8 stars), Apache-2.0 like upstream BoringSSL; usable for benchmarking and study, but the authors themselves say not to use it in production.
